//tmr: The three configuration TMR replicas are keep_hierarchy instances, so a plain flatten leaves $paramod module types that Checker.YosysUnmappedCells counts as unmapped instances and aborts on. deferred_flatten keeps the hierarchy through synthesis and flattens after mapping. tt/src/config.json carries the same key for the same reason.
//dut: The Tiny Tapeout wrapper, not pilot_top, and the choice is deliberate. The IHP reference this run is compared against (docs/15 section 5.3) hardened tt_um_melihakbulut_nssoc inside a fixed 4x2 tile frame from a DEF template. Hardening pilot_top here instead would change the module AND the floorplan style (relative sizing, auto-placed IOs) in the same experiment, so a difference in the result could not be attributed to the PDK. It is also the module the TinyTapeout sky130 GDS action would build, which is the gate this run is checking us against. Source files are read from hw/rtl/ directly rather than from the generated tt/src/ copies so that this run cannot silently harden a stale copy.
//pdk: Both are also passed on the librelane command line by run_sky130.sh: LibreLane's ciel wrapper resolves PDK_ROOT from the CLI option before this file is parsed (docs/12 section 2.4a). sky130A default matches, but it is passed explicitly so the script does not depend on the default staying sky130A.
//clock: 20 ns (50 MHz), byte-identical to the IHP 4x2 run of docs/15 section 5.3 and to the Tiny Tapeout default in tt/src/config.json. Held fixed on purpose: this run varies the PDK and nothing else, so the achieved slack is the portability measurement. sky130_fd_sc_hd is a 1.80 V library with 428 cells against sg13g2's 84 (docs/12 section 5), so if anything it has more resizer freedom at the same constraint, not less.
//tile: The sky130A 4x2 tile, from tt/tt/tech/sky130A/tile_sizes.yaml and the matching pin-frame DEF. Same tile COUNT as the IHP run, different tile SIZE: sky130 4x2 is 682.64 x 225.76 = 154,124 um2 against ihp-sg13g2 4x2 at 854.40 x 313.74 = 268,059 um2. The Tiny Tapeout tile grid is defined per technology, so holding the tile count fixed rather than the die area is the comparison that means something for a shuttle submission. def_suffix is 'pg' on sky130 and 'pgvdd' on ihp-sg13g2 (tt/tt/tech.py), and RT_MAX_LAYER follows project_top_metal_layer: met4 here, TopMetal1 there. These three keys and the PDK/SCL pair are the entire PDK-specific delta against tt/src/config_merged.json. PREREQUISITE: FP_DEF_TEMPLATE resolves into tt/tt/, which is the tt-support-tools clone at commit 01d5d2814fa9dd61e9d211e0b235a4a592a9316a and is GITIGNORED -- it is cloned in by scripts/gen_tt_submission.py, not vendored. A fresh checkout must have that clone in place before this config will run. The reference in tt/src/user_config.json has the same dependency, so this is the project's existing convention rather than a new one; it is named here because a missing template presents as a floorplan error, not as a missing-file error.
//tt: Everything in this block is copied verbatim from the Tiny Tapeout project defaults in tt/src/config.json, which are technology-independent (tt/tt/tech.py gives sky130A an empty librelane_config, so upstream applies no sky130 overrides of its own). Copied rather than referenced so this config is self-contained and diffable against tt/src/config_merged.json.
//signoff: The two keys where this config is deliberately a SUPERSET of the Tiny Tapeout one. tt/src/config.json sets both to 0 under the comment 'Save some time', so the IHP 4x2 run never executed the KLayout deck (docs/15 section 5.3) and only the precheck would have. The docs/12 section 4.1 aer_fifo sign-off ran Magic DRC, the KLayout deck and the Magic/KLayout XOR together, and that is the bar this run is being held to, so both are switched back on here. Netgen LVS and the antenna checks are on by default in the Classic flow and need no key.
//antenna: Explicit, though it is also the LibreLane 3.0.5 default (flows/classic.py). Stated because it is the one antenna knob docs/12 section 4.5 measured rather than assumed on sg13g2 -- 3 diodes off versus 4,641 diodes on for the same zero-violation result -- and because leaving it implicit would make a sky130 diode count unattributable. Note that GRT_REPAIR_ANTENNAS is NOT set here: it is a recognised deprecated alias for RUN_ANTENNA_REPAIR and would change behaviour silently if carried over from a sky130 config written for an older OpenLane (docs/12 section 2.4c). The sibling sky130 project's config does carry it; that is the trap, not the precedent.
//derate: The PDK sets this as the integer 5 and LibreLane's base.sdc and io.tcl consume it with Tcl integer division, so `expr 5 / 100` is 0 and the flow applies NO derate while logging '5%'. Written as a float here so the division is real. docs/28 section 4.4.
//setupcheck: LibreLane resolves a timing checker's corners as <TYPE>_VIOLATION_CORNERS or TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS, and both PDKs ship TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS as ["*typ*"]. With this key unset the setup checker therefore examined the typical corner and nothing else, so the slow corner -- the one that decides whether the part works -- was gated by no checker at all, and four claims that a corner closes were published from runs that did not. HOLD_VIOLATION_CORNERS already ships as ["*"], so only setup was affected. docs/28 section 4.4a. This is the second defect of its shape here: docs/23 records design__violations not aggregating hold. A green checker is only as wide as the corners it was pointed at.
//capslew: Checker.MaxCapViolations and Checker.MaxSlewViolations each declare corner_override = [""] (librelane/steps/checker.py), and TimingViolations.get_corner_variable() turns that into the DEFAULT of MAX_CAP_VIOLATION_CORNERS and MAX_SLEW_VIOLATION_CORNERS. The mechanism is NOT the setup one: [""] is a non-empty list, so the `or` in get_corner_wildcards() is satisfied and these two never fall back to TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS at all. The wildcard list is then filtered of the "" match-none wildcard and comes out empty, no corner is matched, every violation lands in warn_violating_corner, and the step WARNS instead of failing. Neither PDK ships either key -- sky130A resolves both to [""] and sets only TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS = ["*tt*"] -- so the design configuration is the only place that can bind them. docs/18 section 3.3a is where this was first seen on this PDK and read as harmless; docs/34 section 8.5 named it as the third instance of the shape docs/28 section 4.4a describes, and docs/36 closes it. Set here as well as on IHP so the portability comparison keeps comparing configurations that differ only in the PDK-specific keys. WARNING, AND IT IS NOT A REGRESSION: unlike ihp-sg13g2, this design does NOT meet max slew on sky130. The most recent sky130 6x2 run, sky-14-6x2-rcmodel, measures 3,930 max-slew violations across four of the nine corners (1,820 at max_ss_100C_1v60, 1,246 at nom_ss_100C_1v60, 833 at min_ss_100C_1v60, 31 at max_tt_025C_1v80) and still reported flow__errors__count 0 and design__violations 0, because the checker was pointed at no corner. With this key bound, a sky130 re-harden is EXPECTED to end in a deferred FlowError naming Checker.MaxSlewViolations. That is the gate working: sky130 does not close (docs/18 section 3.3 measures the setup miss on the same corners), no sky130 run is part of the TTIHP26b submission, and LibreLane defers this class of error, so the run still completes every step and writes final/ before failing -- the portability measurement is not lost, it is merely no longer reported as clean. Max cap is 0 on all nine corners and that key gates a criterion already met.
